title: 3.5.25 Lab: Objects Capstone — Build, Read, Destructure
description: Build an array of records, read fields with dots and brackets, and destructure a record into variables. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build an array of records
steps.instructions: Create one array (the lesson calls it cart; use any name that fits) whose elements are objects. Give each object the same fields, for example a name, a price and a quantity. Include at least three records.

steps.title: Add a nested object and a spaced key
steps.instructions: Give one record a nested object as a field, and give one record a key that contains a space, written in quotes.

steps.title: Read fields two ways
steps.instructions: Pick one record by its number and print one of its fields with a dot (cart[0].name), and print the spaced key with square brackets. Also read the nested field with a chain (a dot then another dot).

steps.title: Loop and total
steps.instructions: Loop over the array and print each record's name and its cost (price times quantity), reading each field off the record with a dot.

steps.title: Destructure one record
steps.instructions: Destructure two or more fields out of one of the records into variables, in one statement, and use the bare names in a printed sentence.

steps.title: Walk the keys
steps.instructions: Use Object.keys with a loop to print every key and value of one record, fetching each value with brackets. A nested object prints as [object Object] when you join it into text; that is expected here.

requirements.title: array of records built
requirements.description: An array holds object records: written in the brackets or pushed in one at a time. Help: 3.5.2 (Grouping Related Values)
requirements.hint: Make one array with at least three objects in it, and give every object the same kinds of fields.

requirements.title: nested object present
requirements.description: An object literal holds another object literal. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Give one record a field whose value is another object in braces, for example details: { color: "blue" }.

requirements.title: one record's field read with a dot and printed
requirements.description: console.log prints a field of one record picked by its number and read with a dot (cart[0].name), or a variable holding that read. A field printed by the loop in step 4 does not count for this step. Help: 3.5.4 (Reading and Changing Properties)
requirements.hint: Pick one record by its number and print one of its fields with a dot: console.log(cart[0].name).

requirements.title: spaced key read with brackets and printed
requirements.description: console.log prints a value read with square brackets and a quoted key (cart[1]["item code"]), or a variable holding one. Help: 3.5.6 (Square Brackets and Computed Keys)
requirements.hint: A key with a space in it is read with square brackets and the quoted key. Print that read with console.log.

requirements.title: nested field read with a chain and printed
requirements.description: console.log prints a nested field reached with two dots in a row (cart[0].details.color), or a variable holding one. Help: 3.5.10 (A Nested Object Access Chain)
requirements.hint: Reach into the nested object with a chain, one dot after another (the record, the nested field, its field), and print it.

requirements.title: loop works out and prints each cost
requirements.description: A loop over cart (for, while or forEach, on cart or counting to its length) prints each record's price times its quantity: multiplied right in the print, through a variable, through a helper function that returns the product, or from the two read into variables first. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))
requirements.hint: Loop over cart and, inside the loop, print the cost: the record's price times its quantity, each read with a dot (item.price * item.quantity). A helper the loop calls, that prints or returns the cost, counts too: that is checked when you press Run.

requirements.title: destructured names used
requirements.description: Two or more fields are unpacked with a brace pattern, and each bare name is used inside console.log, or in a variable that is then printed. Help: 3.5.19 (Destructuring)
requirements.hint: Put the field names in braces on the left of the equals sign and one record on the right, then print a sentence that uses those names.

requirements.title: Object.keys walked with a loop
requirements.description: A loop goes over Object.keys(...) of one record (cart[0], or a variable holding a record), fetches each value with the key in square brackets, and prints it. Help: 3.5.6 (Square Brackets and Computed Keys)
requirements.hint: Loop over Object.keys(record) with for...of: each key comes out in turn. Inside the loop, print the value fetched with record[key]. for...in is not part of this course, so it does not count here.

requirements.title: output printed
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: cart holds three or more records, one with a nested object and one with a spaced key
requirements.description: After the code runs, cart is an array of at least three objects, one record holds a nested object, one record has a key containing a space, and at least three records have a numeric price and quantity. Help: 3.5.23 (A Record-Shaped Object)
requirements.hint: Build cart with three or more objects. Give one a nested object as a field and one a quoted key with a space in it, and give the records a price and a quantity that are numbers.

checks.expr: Array.isArray(cart) && cart.length >= 3 && cart.every(r => r !== null && typeof r === 'object' && !Array.isArray(r))
checks.fail: cart should be an array of at least three objects, one per record.

checks.expr: cart.some(r => Object.values(r).some(v => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v)))
checks.fail: No record holds a nested object. Give one record a field whose value is another object, like details: { color: "blue" }.
No record has a key with a space in it. Add one, written in quotes, like "item code": "NB-04".
At least three records need a price and a quantity that are numbers (no quotes around them), so the loop can multiply them.

requirements.title: each step's reads are printed by code that runs
requirements.description: Code that runs prints: one record's field read with a dot, the spaced key's value, a nested field reached with a chain, each record's cost from a loop, the unpacked names, and every key and value of one record from a loop; at least eight lines, none undefined or NaN. Text typed in, and prints that never run, do not count. Help: 3.5.23 (A Record-Shaped Object)
requirements.hint: Each print has to read its value from cart and run: not inside a function nobody calls, not behind a test that is never true, and not a typed-in copy of the value.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed by code that runs. A console.log inside a function nobody calls, or behind a test that is never true, prints nothing.
A printed line says undefined: a read found nothing. Check the spelling of each name you read.
Step 3: one record's field, read with a dot, is not printed by code that runs. Pick a record by its number and print a field: console.log(cart[0].name).
Step 3: the value under the key with a space is not printed by code that runs. Read it with brackets and the quoted key: console.log(cart[1]["item code"]).
Step 3: a nested field, reached with a chain of two dots, is not printed by code that runs: console.log(cart[0].details.color).
Step 4: each record's cost (price times quantity) is not printed from the loop. Inside the loop, print the current record's price times its quantity.
Step 5: the unpacked names are not all printed by code that runs. Use each name you unpacked from the record in the printed sentence.
Step 6: no loop prints every key of one record with its value. Loop over Object.keys(cart[0]) and, inside the loop, print the key and cart[0][key].
Fewer than eight lines were printed. Steps 3 to 6 each print: three reads, one line per record, the sentence, and one line per key.
